name: Third-Generation Facilitated Naturalisation

selection_odds.basis: Genuinely low uptake since introduction — approximately 1,868 applications in the first 3 years (2018-2021) against an estimated ~25,000 eligible population

application_window.note: A transitional window for applicants aged 26-35 at the law's 2018 introduction expired 15 February 2023; the standard under-25 route remains open

requirement_groups.name: Standard route (born in Switzerland, applying before age 25)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being born in Switzerland, holding a C permit, having completed at least 5 years of compulsory schooling in Switzerland, and applying before age 25.
This requires at least one grandparent born in Switzerland, or shown to have held a residence right (B, C, L, or A permit, or a carte de légitimation) in Switzerland.
This requires at least one parent who held a C permit, lived in Switzerland for at least 10 years, and completed at least 5 years of compulsory schooling in Switzerland.

evidence_required.document: Documented three-generation family chain (birth certificates, residence records for grandparent and parent)
School records evidencing 5+ years of compulsory schooling in Switzerland

sources.title: Third-generation facilitated naturalisation, Art. 24a SCA - State Secretariat for Migration

notes: GENUINE, CONFIRMED LOW-UPTAKE FINDING: approximately 1,868 applications filed in the first 3 years (2018-2021) against an estimated ~25,000 eligible population — a real and striking gap between statutory eligibility and actual use, worth flagging prominently as a genuine 'route exists but is rarely used' case, distinct from every other route in this dataset. Introduced by Art. 24a SCA (in force 15 February 2018), itself approved by a genuinely narrow 60.4% referendum result (12 February 2017) — a real democratic-legitimacy data point worth noting given Switzerland's direct-democracy system, not replicated for any other citizenship reform elsewhere in this dataset. Requires documenting THREE generations of family history (grandparent + parent + applicant) — a genuinely more demanding evidentiary burden than most other ancestry routes in this dataset, which typically require documentation of only one or two generations. A transitional window that allowed applicants aged 26-35 at the law's introduction to also apply EXPIRED 15 February 2023 — this route as currently encoded reflects only the standard, ongoing under-25 pathway.
